newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Former Apple exec returns.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Former Apple exec returns.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Friday announced plans to acquire NeXT Software Inc for $400 million. The computer maker also said former Apple executive Rick LeFaivre is returning to the company. The following is a copy of the company's statement.

CUPERTINO, Calif., Dec. 20 /PRNewswire/ -- Apple Computer, Inc. today announced that Dr. Rick LeFaivre, 49, has returned to the company as vice president of the newly formed Apple Technology Group. LeFaivre was formerly vice president of Apple's Advanced Technology Group, and most recently was senior vice president and chief technology officer at Computer Curriculum Corporation, a subsidiary of Viacom, Inc. He will report to Ellen Hancock, executive vice president of research and development and chief technology officer.
The Apple Technology Group will house Apple's research laboratories, human interface technologies and advanced systems architecture, offering support for hardware and software integration.
"Rick was a highly respected technology executive during his first tenure at Apple, and I am excited that he has chosen to return to the team," said Hancock.
"Apple is fully committed to remaining an innovator in the computer industry, and the Apple Technology Group is critical to our future success."

"Apple Computer is a unique company," said LeFaivre. "I've been away for a year and a half and found that I truly missed the excitement and passion of the company, its employees and products. I am really looking forward to my participation in moving the company into the 21st century by building that future with the work we are doing today in our labs."

LeFaivre has held R&D management positions at Sun Microsystems and Silicon Graphics Computer Systems, in addition to Apple Computer and Viacom. He is also a former professor of computer science at Rutgers, the State University of New Jersey.
LeFaivre holds his B.A. in mathematics from the University of Missouri, Columbia, and his M.S. and Ph.D. in computer sciences from the University of Wisconsin, Madison.
